SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    orders.status AS "orders.status",
    COUNT(*) AS "orders.orders",
    COUNT(DISTINCT orders.customer_id) AS "orders.customers"
  FROM orders AS orders
  GROUP BY
    orders.status
), _cm_orders__customers__credit_sum AS (
  SELECT
    _base."customers.orders.status" AS "customers.orders.status",
    CAST(SUM(_base._v) AS DOUBLE) AS "customers.credit_sum_host"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      orders.status AS "customers.orders.status",
      customers.id AS _ek0,
      MAX(customers.credit) AS _v
    FROM customers AS customers
    LEFT JOIN orders AS orders
      ON customers.id = orders.customer_id
    WHERE
      NOT customers.id IS NULL
    GROUP BY
      orders.status,
      customers.id
  ) AS _base
  GROUP BY
    _base."customers.orders.status"
)
SELECT
  _base."orders.status",
  _cm_orders__customers__credit_sum."customers.credit_sum_host" AS "orders.total_credit",
  _base."orders.orders",
  _base."orders.customers"
FROM _base
LEFT JOIN _cm_orders__customers__credit_sum
  ON _base."orders.status" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_orders__customers__credit_sum."customers.orders.status"
LIMIT 21

args.message: For each order status, I added up the credit limits of the customers who have at least one order with that status. Each customer is counted once per status, so a customer with many orders isn't counted more than once. "bad": 92,580 (169 customers, 606 orders). "ok": 111,230 (201 customers, 4,410 orders). A customer with orders in both statuses is counted under each, so the two totals overlap and shouldn't be added together.
